newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Cricket-West Indies 266 for six at tea v Australia.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-West Indies 266 for six at tea v Australia.

text.p: West Indies were 266 for six at tea on the final day of the first test against Australia at the Gabba on Tuesday after losing three wickets in the second session of play.
A century by opener Sherwin Campbell was the only bright spot for West Indies, who now have virtually no hope of reaching the winning target of 420 set for them by Australia.
Campbell was 108 at the interval after batting for almost six hours. All too often Campbell went without adequate support as wickets fell at regular intervals throughout the day.
Pace bowler Ian Bishop was the other not out batsman on 13.
Shivnarine Chanderpaul, who scored 82 in the first innings, was bowled by Glenn McGrath for 14 before leg-spinner Shane Warne trapped Jimmy Adams leg before wicket for two.
Courtney Browne was the third wicket to fall in the afternoon session, caught behind by Ian Healy off McGrath's bowling for 20.

Resuming at 89 for one at the start of play, West Indies lost the decisive wicket of Brian Lara for 44 to Paul Reiffel early in the day. Carl Hooper, who scored a century in the first innings, then fell to part-time spinner Michael Bevan for 23.
McGrath had 2-56 from 25 overs and Warne 2-78 from 35 overs.
